questions.q: True or false? With the ball on the left, the midfield slides a few steps but still covers the middle.
questions.explain: Right, it's true. A short slide keeps the group connected, so a pass inside still meets a midfielder.
choiceExplanations: Right, it's true. A short slide keeps the group connected, so a pass inside still meets a midfielder.
Look at the central midfielder: the group slid left together, but he still guards the middle.

questions.q: The ball has switched to the right. Which midfield shape protects against the next pass?
options: Midfield stays in its central spots
Midfield slides right as a group
All three midfielders go to the ball
questions.explain: Yes. Sliding together puts help near the ball while the middle stays covered.
choiceExplanations: The group has not followed the danger, so the carrier's side is short of help.
Yes. Sliding together puts help near the ball while the middle stays covered.
Everyone chases the ball, so one pass inside or across finds the empty middle.

questions.q: The ball is on the right, but your left midfielder stayed out wide. Drag him where he helps.
options: Stay wide on the left touchline
questions.explain: Yes. Tucking in closes the gap beside the central midfielder, so a pass inside is covered.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Tucking in closes the gap beside the central midfielder, so a pass inside is covered.
Alone out wide, he leaves a big gap in midfield for the next pass through the middle.
Chasing across leaves the whole left side and middle empty if the ball is switched back.
